used_clauses:
Use the symmetric model $M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], the
basic field subspace $V$ of the vacuum Fock space spanned by the restricted
lower vectors $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
and the bilinear form $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu,\nu}$. Define the **standard
coordinate functional** $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ in the restricted integral
weight dual of the lower lattice by
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$. The restriction of $B$ to $V$ is
nondegenerate; identify its field dual with $V$ via $B$ and denote by
$\pi(M_\mu)$ the vector representing $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, equivalently the
$B$-orthogonal projection of $M_\mu$ onto $V$. This is the definition of $\pi$
used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition.
If $G^*(\lambda)$ is the $B$-dual upper vector, then
$$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\ \mathrm{restricted}} d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\,G^*(\lambda).$$
At each content the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of
the upper dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient
minor. The full family of raw $M_\mu$ is the basis of the ambient standard
lattice; the full projected family $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is generally
redundant. The projection $\pi$ need not land in the lower integral lattice. In
$e=2$ one has $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$ and
$G_{11}^*=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$, exhibiting the possible field denominator.
The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the
declared global-basis suppliers.

[F2] The restricted lower vectors expand as
$G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ with $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}\in
q\mathbb Z[q]$, equal to $1$ at $\mu=\lambda$ and vanishing unless $\mu$ is
strictly dominated by $\lambda$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
[[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).

used_clauses:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.

[F3] The transition polynomials $d_{\lambda,\mu}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$ are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=m$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

used_clauses:
In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ and every partition $\mu$ of content $\alpha$, the
graded decomposition polynomial factors as
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\,d_{\nu,\mu}(q),$$
where $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ are the adjustment polynomials of
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]] and
$d_{\nu,\mu}$ the characteristic-independent global-basis transition polynomial
of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[J(\nu)]=[D(\nu)]+\sum_{\lambda\lhd\nu}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$. In
particular the characteristic-$p$ decomposition matrix is the product of the
dominance-unitriangular adjustment matrix and the (characteristic-independent)
matrix of global-basis coefficients, and no claim is made that the adjustment
matrix is the identity. Choice is inherited only through the transported
global-basis suppliers.

[F1] The Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors: $[S(\mu)]$ maps to
$S_\mu$ under $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]), and
$S_\mu=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}d_{\nu,\mu}(q)D_\nu$ in the upper family
([[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]]), with the
transition polynomials of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].
